title: Grumblegut Under-Bridge Leaf Loaf
tagline: Forty crunchy leaves, one wellington boot, and absolutely no manners.
servings: Serves one troll family and their cousin
steps:
Stuff the boot with leaves until it burps and groans,
Then sit on the lid and give three troll moans.

Tip in the puddle, so brown and so deep,
And stir with a twig till the lumps start to creep.

Knot up the gloves with the string in a bow,
They're the drumsticks, you see, so wiggle them so.

Sprinkle compost crumbs thick, like a grubby snowfall,
Then bake in a hollow oak, nowhere at all.

Carve with a spade at the stroke of half-two,
And serve to your cousin who's stuck to your shoe.
rhyme:
Into the pot goes a boot, left and sloppy,
With forty damp leaves all gooey and floppy!
Add a bucket of puddle, all brown and all slurpy,
Then a bogey-green glove that goes burpy-burpy!
Twist in some twigs that are furry with mould,
And a sock-coloured string that's a hundred years old!
Sprinkle some crumbs from the compost heap's floor,
Stir it up, stir it up, grumble and snore!
Troll family, troll family, gather to dine,
Elbows on table and wellies in line!
image_prompt: A huge lumpy brown loaf shaped like a wellington boot, crammed with soggy autumn leaves poking out, sitting on a chipped platter. Two chewed gardening gloves rest on top like drumsticks, tied with hairy string. Muddy puddle gravy pools around twigs and compost crumbs, with a rusty tin lid beside.
alt_text: A boot-shaped loaf stuffed with soggy leaves, topped with two old gardening gloves, surrounded by muddy puddle gravy, twigs and a rusty lid.
caption_hook:
Troll Thanksgiving is a sensitive time of year. Someone always cries into the gravy, and it's usually the boot.

Who in your family would demand the second helping of leaf loaf?
